   1 +-- =============================================================================
   2 +-- Migration 0259: version and lifecycle for every installable extension
   3 +--
   4 +-- Why    : 0096 gives a plugin one `version` column and a three-value status,
   5 +--          so publishing, deprecating and rolling back are all DB migrations.
   6 +--          There is no record of what a plugin was before its current version,
   7 +--          which means rollback has nothing to roll back TO, and no way to stop
   8 +--          one bad version without withdrawing the whole entry. Connectors,
   9 +--          skills and MCP servers carry no version at all, so "all are
  10 +--          versioned" was true of exactly one of the four.
  11 +--
  12 +-- Versions: `plugin_registry_versions` is the history the entry points into.
  13 +--          Each row carries its own status and artifact, so a single bad
  14 +--          version is suspended fleet-wide while the rest stay installable, and
  15 +--          rollback repoints the entry at the newest still-published version.
  16 +--          The entry keeps its `version` column as the CURRENT pointer, so
  17 +--          every existing reader keeps working unchanged.
  18 +--
  19 +-- Lifecycle: draft -> in_review -> published, and from published either
  20 +--          deprecated (installable, discouraged) or suspended (not installable,
  21 +--          and existing installs stop). Both are reversible by republishing,
  22 +--          which is why nothing is deleted. The LIFECYCLE LIVES ON THE VERSION,
  23 +--          not on the entry: `PluginRegistryStatus` in the shared contract has
  24 +--          three values, and widening the entry's column past them would make
  25 +--          every catalogue read throw. An entry whose current version is
  26 +--          suspended reads as `deprecated`, which is the existing value that
  27 +--          already means do not install.
  28 +--
  29 +-- Audit  : `plugin_registry_lifecycle_events` records who moved a version and
  30 +--          why. An admin action that stops other people's installs must be
  31 +--          attributable; the previous mechanism, a migration, at least had a
  32 +--          commit to point at.
  33 +--
  34 +-- Backfill: every existing entry gets one version row matching what it already
  35 +--          serves, so the history is never empty for a plugin that exists.
  36 +--
  37 +-- Depends: 0048 (user_connectors), 0096 (plugin_registry_entries),

   1 +-- =============================================================================
   2 +-- Migration 0266: a durable receipt for every browser, computer-use and

  15 +-- provider side in two explicit halves (what we estimated at settle time and

  18 +-- existed keep their history rather than being invented.

  20 +-- customer_credits is the same money in the unit a user sees. One credit is a

  31 +## Jev Decisions
  32 +
  33 +Coding agents delegate explicit task classification, skill selection, prioritization,
  34 +and implementation approach choices to Jev through `pnpm -s agent:decide`.
  35 +Read the installed [TypeSafe skill](../../.agents/skills/typesafe-ai/SKILL.md) when
  36 +preparing questions. Gather evidence and reasonable alternatives, let Jev select,
  37 +then implement and verify the selection. Do not frame the options to rubber-stamp
  38 +a preferred answer. Batch independent questions sharing the same evidence; ask
  39 +dependent questions after their prerequisite answers or new evidence are available.
  40 +
  41 +The helper reads `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` from the process environment, or from the
  42 +repository-root `.env.local` if the environment variable is absent. It reads that
  43 +file as data, uses only the key, and never prints it. Keep it out of tracked files.
  44 +The official SDK supplies the endpoint and default model; this developer helper
  45 +rejects endpoint/model environment overrides and does not change product routing.
  46 +
  47 +Pass a JSON object on stdin with `state` and named `questions`. Each question has
  48 +`type: "choice"`, meaningful `instructions`, and descriptive `criteria`, including
  49 +`no_suitable_choice`. Question IDs are response keys; include the complete meaning
  50 +in instructions because Jev does not see the IDs. Example:
  51 +
  52 +```sh
  53 +pnpm -s agent:decide <<'JSON'
  54 +{
  55 +  "state": {
  56 +    "goal": "Choose the next investigation.",
  57 +    "evidence": "An isolated test reproduces acceptance of expired sessions. Another test reports a heading spacing mismatch."
  58 +  },
  59 +  "questions": {
  60 +    "next_investigation": {
  61 +      "type": "choice",
  62 +      "instructions": "Which investigation should be prioritized given the observed failures?",
  63 +      "criteria": {
  64 +        "session_expiry": "Investigate acceptance of expired sessions.",
  65 +        "heading_spacing": "Investigate the heading spacing mismatch.",
  66 +        "no_suitable_choice": "The evidence does not justify selecting either investigation."
  67 +      }
  68 +    }
  69 +  }
  70 +}
  71 +JSON
  72 +```
  73 +
  74 +Only the supplied state and questions are sent to TypeSafe using the developer's
  75 +account. Send the minimum relevant evidence; never send credentials, environment
  76 +file contents, customer data, or Local/BYOK session content through this helper.
  77 +It does not read repository content automatically or execute the selected action.
  78 +
  79 +The JSON result includes each choice, probabilities, confidence, actual model,
  80 +token usage, and a hash of the input including any local confidence policy.
  81 +Report Jev's choice and confidence when the decision materially affects the work.
  82 +Keep evidence freshness in view: a selection applies to the state submitted.
  83 +
  84 +When invoked directly with `node scripts/jev-decide.mjs`, exit code `0` means all
  85 +choices were selected, `2` means at least one choice needs review, and `1` means
  86 +the request failed. The pnpm script wrapper may normalize nonzero exit codes to
  87 +`1`; consume the JSON `status` to distinguish review from failure. Abstention or
  88 +tied leading options pause the affected choice. A question may specify
  89 +`minimumConfidence` between 0 and 1;
  90 +derive that policy from evaluated cases and consequences, not an invented universal
  91 +threshold. A result below that threshold also needs review. On malformed answers,
  92 +missing credentials, service failure, or exhausted time/retry budgets, report the
  93 +failure and pause the affected choice. Gather missing evidence or ask the user;
  94 +never silently substitute the coding agent's choice or retry until a preferred
  95 +answer appears. Independent work may continue.
  96 +
  97 +Explicit user instructions, repository rules, permissions, deterministic checks,
  98 +and observed facts govern execution. Jev does not authorize actions or replace
  99 +tests, and confidence is not proof of correctness. This is an agent workflow
 100 +instruction, not an interceptor that can force every internal model decision or
 101 +tool call through Jev. The helper validates its own requests and responses.
 102 +
 103 +Operational limits live in `scripts/config/jev-decisions.json`. Run
 104 +`pnpm test:agent-decisions` for offline validation; the example above makes a paid
 105 +live API call. SDK logging is disabled and raw provider errors are not echoed.
